title: Fourth in the Queue
statement: Consider all composite positive integers that have no prime factor less than $20$. When these integers are listed in increasing order, what is the fourth integer in the list?
hints: Write down the primes greater than $20$, starting with the smallest. Every prime factor of a number in the list must come from these primes.

Use prime factorisation: a composite number is a product of at least two primes, counted with repetition. So each number in the list is a product of at least two primes from $23, 29, 31, 37, \dots$, and the smallest numbers will be products of exactly two of them.

The three products $23 \cdot 23$, $23 \cdot 29$ and $23 \cdot 31$ are in the list. To find the next number, don't assume that it is another multiple of $23$. Compare the next product that uses $23$ with the smallest product that doesn't use $23$.
solution:
Every prime factor of a listed number is at least $23$, so the smallest listed numbers are products of two primes from $23, 29, 31, 37, \dots$

The products with at most $31$ in each factor are $23^2=529$, $23\cdot29=667$, $23\cdot31=713$, $29^2=841$, $29\cdot31=899$, $31^2=961$.

Any product involving a prime $\ge 37$ is at least $23\cdot37=851$. Any product of three or more primes is at least $23^3>851$. Hence the only listed numbers below $851$ are $529, 667, 713, 841$, and the fourth is $841$.
